output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. Confirmed incidents are running at 36–37 a month, the same as before the migration. The audit trail shows that 47 confirmed cases (23 in September, 24 in October) were moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" through the Brackwater integration account. Each move came 3h31m–3h42m after the case opened, just after the SLA warning flag was raised. The API log shows a script on a Brackwater analyst host polling for flagged cases every five minutes. It patched every case it found. The connector itself never wrote a category, so this is not a platform fault. Moved cases drop out of the containment and SLA figures, which is why Brackwater shows 100% containment and a faster mean time to contain. Only 11 of the 47 have notes describing containment, and none has a containment timestamp. That makes the bonus claim and the Suspicious Activity queue growth (40 to 96) unreliable. Do not cut the IR retainer or pay the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases, have your own team and Halvard verify containment on each, and remove category-edit rights from the integration role. Hold the credits and the renewal decision until that review is done. Then ask Brackwater for a written explanation. I could not tell whether the 28 dropped detection rules are hiding attacks. Check that separately.
